newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: SKI JUMPING-SLOVENIA'S PETERKA CLAIMS OVERALL TITLE.
newsitem.headline: SKI JUMPING-SLOVENIA'S PETERKA CLAIMS OVERALL TITLE.

text.p: Slovenian teenager Primoz Peterka sealed victory in the overall ski jumping World Cup on Saturday with a fourth place in the season's penultimate event.

Peterka, 18 and in only his second winter on the World Cup tour, leads the overall standings with an unbeatable 1,322 points to German Dieter Thoma's 1,190 after the first of back-to-back ski flying competitions at this northern Slovenian resort.
The day's victory went to Japan's Takanobu Okabe who posted jumps of 197.50 metres and 207 metres -- the longest-ever ski flying jump recorded in World Cup competition.
Okabe's compatriot Kazuyoshi Funaki, currently third in the standings, took second place with jumps of 190.50 and 204 metres, ahead of Finland's Jani Soininen who sailed to 203.50 and 187 metres.
In training earlier on Saturday, Norway's Lasse Ottesen broke his compatriot Espen Brdesen's 1994 world ski flying record of 209 metres when he soared to 212 metres.

Despite clinching the overall title in front of an overjoyed home crowd of 80,000, Peterka, an economics student, was disappointed with his fourth place on Saturday after jumps of 196.50 and 186 metres.
